clue.text: Prepared strudels left out ready for the oven?

indicators.note: prepared in the sense of worked up or made over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
left out means the letter for left is dropped from the pastry word

explanation.surface: A baker has made some strudels and set them aside, ready to be baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' drops L from STRUDELS, leaving STRUDES, which 'Prepared' rearranges. The strudels belong to the surface; the oven-ready thing is a tied-up bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry is tied with string before roasting, so a bird bound that way is ready to be cooked.

clue.text: Cutting back on exercises, taking black taxi

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for cutting from right to left

parts.note: a cutting remark is an acid one, sharp and caustic
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone trims their gym routine and hails a black cab instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like trimming the workout; it is the adjective for a sharp remark, and 'back' turns that word round before the black letter ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw that carries paying passengers, a kind of cycle taxi.

clue.text: Type of tyre rapidly moulded on a hub of aluminium

indicators.note: a tyre is fitted on a hub, so the shuffled letters go around the metal's symbol
moulded means shaped anew, so the letters of rapidly are reworked

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A tyre is quickly formed and fitted onto an aluminium wheel hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moulded' rearranges the speed word into RADIPLY, and 'on a hub of' fits that around the metal's symbol, as a tyre sits on a wheel hub.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial-ply tyre has its cord plies running at right angles to the tread, a standard construction for car tyres.

clue.text: Top-up to wages attracting British duty

parts.note: an onus is a duty or responsibility

explanation.surface: An extra payment to workers ends up being subject to a British tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' looks like a tax, chiming with wages, but here it means an obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra sum paid on top of normal earnings, often as a reward.

clue.text: Tough stuff from Prokofiev, say

definitions.meaning: a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric used for uniforms and suits
the composer Prokofiev used the French form of his first name, Sergei, in the West; 'say' marks him as one example

explanation.surface: Something hard-going comes from the Russian composer Prokofiev.
explanation.walkthrough: Prokofiev published in the West as Serge Prokofieff, so the French form of Sergei is fair here; 'say' shows he is just one person with the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable twilled cloth, so it is tough material; it is also a first name, the one Prokofiev used in France.

clue.text: Bring about the return of US soldier into home country

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: into tells us the turned soldier goes inside the word for country

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

indicators.note: the return of means the soldier's letters go back the other way

parts.note: GI is the familiar term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone prompts an American soldier to come back into his home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the return of' turns the soldier round to IG, and 'into' places that inside the nation word, with 'home' supplying the opening two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going or cause it to happen.

clue.text: Explanatory note giving the purpose of landlord's policy?

definitions.meaning: a letter sent with a document or application to explain it

definitions.text: giving the purpose of landlord's policy?
definitions.meaning: a landlord is one who lets, so an insurance policy protecting him is read as protecting the one who lets

explanation.surface: A note explains what a landlord's insurance policy is meant to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as 'covering' (insuring) plus 'letter' (one who lets property, a landlord).
explanation.definitionFit: A letter sent alongside a CV or enclosure to introduce and explain it is a standard name for such an accompanying note.

clue.text: Artist with no patron suffering removal

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist without a patron goes through hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges ARTIST + NO + PATRON, with 'with' only joining them. 'no patron' reads as a phrase but supplies two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Transportation was the historical punishment of shipping convicts to a penal colony, a forced removal from the country.

clue.text: Disagree with what child kidnappers will do

definitions.meaning: to raise an objection or dispute a point
issue means offspring, so kidnappers of a child literally seize someone's issue

explanation.surface: Someone disputes what child abductors are going to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is a formal word for children, so the second reading is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with someone is to dispute or challenge what they say, a set idiom for disagreeing.

clue.text: Reported widespread hatred for classical theatre

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so we want a word that is said like another

parts.note: odium is general hatred or public disgust

explanation.surface: Word is that a classical theatre is broadly despised.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome an odeum was a roofed building for musical performances, a classical theatre.

clue.text: Store firm opened up by roundabout

indicators.note: opened up by means the firm word is split to admit the ring shape

parts.note: hard means firm or solid
a roundabout is a circle, and O is circular

explanation.surface: A shop that is a solid concern gets opened up by a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' and 'Store' both look like businesses; here firm is an adjective and the roundabout is just the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile of things kept back, so as a verb or noun it means a store.

clue.text: Top of the range champion dog breed

parts.note: a ridge is the crest of a mountain range
to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A dog of excellent quality wins its breed category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the range' looks like advertising talk for the best, and 'champion' like a show winner; they are a crest and a verb for supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a hound named for the ridge of hair along its back, a recognised breed.

clue.text: Old disc given a spin in former audio download

indicators.note: in places the old letter and the turned disc inside the word for former

parts.note: past means former, gone by

indicators.note: a spin turns the disc round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: CD, compact disc

explanation.surface: An old record is played in the days before audio downloads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a spin' turns CD into DC; with O that goes 'in' PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is a recorded audio programme that listeners download or stream.

clue.text: Hunting cat traps large snake

indicators.note: traps means holds inside, so the size letter goes within the hunter

parts.note: a ratter is an animal, cat or dog, kept for catching rats
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A hunting cat catches a big snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunting cat' looks like a big cat; it is a ratter, an animal that hunts rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is the informal name for a rattlesnake.

clue.text: Songbird — tons pipe down around river

indicators.note: around means the quiet word wraps the river letter

parts.note: pipe down means be quiet, as does hush

explanation.surface: A songbird is told to stop its tons of piping down by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' suggests birdsong, but 'pipe down' is a command to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a familiar songbird, such as the song thrush or mistle thrush.

clue.text: Stand directly below green for drivers

parts.note: under means directly beneath
a green traffic light tells drivers to go

explanation.surface: A golfer stands right under the green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' and 'drivers' suggest golf; the drivers are motorists at traffic lights.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to endure it, and to undergo is likewise to go through or bear an experience.

clue.text: Being such as settles in random places?

definitions.text: Being such as settles in random places?

indicators.note: in random places puts the letters anywhere, a sign to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A person who sets up home just anywhere has no fixed nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in random places' rearranges AS SETTLES. The whole clue also describes such a person: one who settles anywhere belongs to no country.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without any citizenship has no nation of their own and so settles wherever they can.

clue.text: Mostly put out about risen and not forbidden double-dealing

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word wraps around the next pieces
mostly means all but the final letter of the word for put out

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out
something that has risen is up
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Someone largely irritated by an uprising, and by things being allowed, is two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts DOUSE to DOUS, which goes 'about' UP and LICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicitous means deceitful or two-faced, practising double-dealing.

clue.text: Appeal to higher authority that's no right to be profitable

indicators.note: that's no right means the letter for right is missing from the appeal word

parts.note: to pray is to appeal to God, the highest authority

explanation.surface: Going to a higher court on appeal earns money if you have no right to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher authority' suggests a court of appeal; it is God, so the appeal is a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: When a venture pays, it brings in a return, as in 'crime doesn't pay'.

clue.text: Name a current Gulf state

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Give a name to a country by the Persian Gulf that is up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day'; it is the physics symbol I for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the United Arab Emirates, a state on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Meeting continued to do something

parts.note: to act is to do something

explanation.surface: A meeting carried on so that someone would take action.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact means a meeting or coming together, as when two things touch.

clue.text: Risk limiting demand on railway and hamper construction?

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the wager word goes around the request

parts.note: a bet is a risk or wager
to ask is to demand

explanation.surface: Risking higher railway charges might obstruct building work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' reads as a verb meaning obstruct; here it is the wicker basket, so the construction is basket-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketry is the craft of weaving wicker items, the making of things such as picnic baskets.

clue.text: Gifted musician cracked head register, losing a repeated note

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing means one copy of the note is removed from the phrase

parts.note: E is a musical note, and it appears more than once in the phrase

explanation.surface: A talented singer's voice breaks in the high register, missing one of the notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes one E (the note occurring three times in HEAD REGISTER), and 'cracked' rearranges what is left. 'head register' and 'cracked' suggest a singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight-reader can play music straight from the score on first sight, a skill of an accomplished musician.

clue.text: Go out with one lost wanderer with little time for socialising

indicators.note: with one lost means the numeral letter is dropped from the leaving word

parts.note: to exit is to go out
I is the Roman numeral one
a rover is a wanderer
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A lone wanderer with hardly any time to mix leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes I from EXIT. The surface describes a loner, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing person is all for company, so the adjective describes someone keen on mixing with others.

clue.text: Darn situation leading to someone's disadvantage?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, a state of being stitched, since darning is stitching
a set-up or frame contrived to put someone in the wrong

explanation.surface: A wretched situation that ends badly for somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn' looks like a mild curse; it is the mending verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is a frame or fix that unfairly incriminates or disadvantages someone; read literally it is a sewing-up.

clue.text: A week on location in the NHS is difficult to deal with

parts.note: a ward is a room in a hospital, such as those run by the NHS

explanation.surface: A week spent on a hospital ward is tough to cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, which runs public hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awkward is hard to handle or manage, like an awkward customer.

clue.text: Completely finished swapping parts for umbrella

indicators.note: swapping parts tells us to put the two halves of the phrase the other way round

parts.note: over means finished
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: An umbrella is entirely done for after its parts are exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely finished' gives ALL OVER, and 'swapping parts' reverses the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella term covers everything, as an overall figure is comprehensive.

clue.text: One who cures sickroom outbreak with elixir taken externally

indicators.note: taken externally means only the outside letters of each word are used

explanation.surface: A healer deals with an outbreak in the sickroom using an elixir applied to the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken externally' picks S-M, O-K and E-R from the outsides of sickroom, outbreak and elixir. The surface suggests healing, but these cures are of bacon or fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure meat or fish is to preserve it, and smoking is one method, so a smoker cures food.

clue.text: Character behind hotel in area of dense population

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter after Hotel stands for I
a country with well over a billion people

explanation.surface: A character waits behind a hotel in a crowded district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter, and 'hotel' its name in the NATO alphabet used in radio.
explanation.definitionFit: The country's name is the code word for I in radio spelling, and it is also among the most populous nations.

clue.text: In truth, routine one finds boring

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the next word

explanation.surface: Honestly, any routine becomes tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in a groove means a dull, unvarying routine.
